findings.title: [P1] Restore socket-listener removal in the disposer
findings.body: When a caller invokes the returned disposer, subsequent messages still invoke the handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles therefore accumulate stale listeners, retain associated state, and duplicate message processing, contrary to the existing cleanup contract.

findings.title: [P1] Clear the polling interval in the disposer
findings.body: After a caller invokes the returned cleanup function, `refresh` continues running every second. Repeated start/cleanup cycles accumulate timers and retained closures, and a live interval can prevent Node.js from exiting.

findings.title: [P2] Restore socket-listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
Calling the disposer no longer detaches the `"message"` handler. Any message received afterward invokes stale handlers; repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners, causing duplicate processing, retained state, and eventual listener-leak warnings.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore interval cancellation in the polling disposer
findings.body:
Calling the returned stop function leaves the interval active. Poll callbacks continue after cancellation, repeated start/stop cycles create unbounded concurrent polling, and in Node.js the referenced intervals can keep the process alive indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
After callers invoke the disposer, subsequent `"message"` events still call the handler. Reattaching also accumulates duplicate listeners, causing stale processing and memory leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Clear the polling interval in the returned disposer
findings.body:
Calling the disposer no longer stops polling. `refresh` continues every second indefinitely, repeated starts accumulate timers, and in Node.js the live interval can prevent process shutdown.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore message-listener removal during cleanup
findings.body:
On a long-lived or reused socket, calling the returned cleanup function no longer detaches the handler. A remote peer sending a message after logout, session teardown, or ownership transfer can therefore trigger stale logic with the previous session’s state or privileges.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
After `attach()` returns, calling its cleanup function no longer unregisters the handler. Any socket that outlives a component/request continues invoking stale handlers; repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate listeners, retained state, and duplicate message processing.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval during cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function leaves the interval running forever. Each start/cleanup cycle adds another periodic callback, retaining its closure and multiplying work; in Node.js, the referenced interval can also prevent the process from exiting.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
